tool_arguments.query: Broadcom AI semiconductor revenue Q2 fiscal 2026 custom accelerators XPUs networking

events.content: Broadcom AI semiconductor revenue Q2 fiscal 2026 custom accelerators XPUs networking

**Broadcom’s Q2 FY2026 AI semiconductor revenue was $10.8 billion**, up **143% year over year**, driven by demand for **custom AI accelerators (XPUs)** and **AI networking**; the fiscal quarter ended **May 3, 2026**. [[1, 2]] 

This result was modestly above Broadcom’s Q1 outlook for **$10.7 billion** in Q2 AI semiconductor revenue, an outperformance of roughly **$0.1 billion (0.9%)**. [[3]] 

For context, Q2 semiconductor-solutions revenue was **$15.009 billion**, meaning AI semiconductors represented about **72.0%** of the segment; total company revenue was **$22.187 billion**, making AI semiconductor revenue approximately **48.7%** of consolidated sales. [[1, 2]] 

Broadcom guided Q3 FY2026 AI semiconductor revenue to **$16.0 billion**, implying more than **200% year-over-year growth** and roughly **48% sequential growth** from Q2. [[1]] 

The key takeaway is that Broadcom’s AI revenue category encompasses both the **custom accelerator/XPU silicon** deployed by hyperscalers and the **networking components** required to scale those accelerator clusters; the company did not disclose a Q2 revenue split between the two categories. [[1]]

tool_arguments.query: Broadcom FY2025 full year AI semiconductor revenue from 10-K annual filing

events.content: Broadcom FY2025 full year AI semiconductor revenue from 10-K annual filing

Broadcom’s fiscal 2025 ended **November 2, 2025**—not at the end of November—because its fiscal year ends on the Sunday closest to October 31. [[1]] 

For FY2025, Broadcom reported **$20.0 billion of AI semiconductor revenue**, up **65% year over year**, according to CEO Hock Tan’s year-end earnings-call remarks. [[2]] 

That AI revenue was generated principally from **custom AI accelerators (XPUs) and AI networking**, while Broadcom’s reported Semiconductor Solutions segment revenue was **$36.858 billion**, up 22% year over year. [[1]] [[3]] 

Thus, AI semiconductor revenue represented approximately **54.3%** of FY2025 Semiconductor Solutions revenue ($20.0bn ÷ $36.858bn). [[2]] [[1]] 

For context, Broadcom reported total FY2025 revenue of **$63.887 billion**, including **$36.858 billion** in Semiconductor Solutions and **$27.029 billion** in Infrastructure Software. [[1]] 

There is **no FY2026 annual report yet** as of October 17, 2026: Broadcom had reported through fiscal Q3 ended August 2, 2026, and guided Q4 to end November 1, 2026. [[4]] 

Based on reported FY2026 quarterly AI semiconductor revenue of **$8.4 billion in Q1**, **$10.8 billion in Q2**, and **$16.7 billion in Q3**, plus the company’s **$21.7 billion Q4 forecast**, FY2026 AI semiconductor revenue would total approximately **$57.6 billion if Q4 guidance is achieved**; this is an estimate, not an annual-report result. [[5]] [[6]] [[4]]

tool_arguments.query: Broadcom Q1 FY2026 earnings call AI semiconductor revenue custom accelerator XPU networking breakdown

events.content: Broadcom Q1 FY2026 earnings call AI semiconductor revenue custom accelerator XPU networking breakdown

**Broadcom’s “AI semiconductor revenue” is a management-reported revenue category rather than a separately reported GAAP operating segment; it refers principally to sales of (1) customer-specific AI compute accelerators—called custom AI accelerators or XPUs—and (2) AI networking products.** [[1]] [[2]]

**XPU** is Broadcom management’s umbrella term for the purpose-built computing accelerators it supplies for customers’ AI data centers; these are customized alternatives to general-purpose GPU-based compute, exemplified in the call by shipments of Google’s Ironwood TPU and OpenAI’s Jalapeno accelerator. [[3]] [[2]]

**Custom accelerator revenue** therefore means revenue from these customer-designed or customer-tailored AI chips, while **AI networking revenue** encompasses the high-bandwidth interconnect needed to link AI accelerators—particularly Ethernet switching and optical interconnect products. [[2]] [[3]] 

For fiscal Q3 2026, ended August 2, 2026, Broadcom reported **$16.7 billion** of AI semiconductor revenue, up **221% year over year** and **54% sequentially**. [[1]] 

Management said XPU shipments increased by more than **3.5× year over year** and represented **73%** of Q3 AI revenue, while AI-networking revenue rose more than **2.5× year over year**. [[2]] 

This AI category was the principal growth driver within Broadcom’s Semiconductor Solutions segment, whose Q3 revenue was **$20.839 billion**, up **127% year over year**; total company revenue was **$29.591 billion**. [[1]] 

For fiscal Q4 2026, Broadcom guided to **$21.7 billion** of AI semiconductor revenue, implying **236% year-over-year growth**, and management’s Q3-call outlook was approximately **$58 billion** of AI revenue for full-year fiscal 2026. [[1]] [[3]] 

In short, the phrase should be read as Broadcom’s combined AI-chip platform revenue—**custom XPU/ASIC compute plus the Ethernet/optical fabric that scales those systems**—not as revenue from a single standalone “AI semiconductor” product or a formal reported segment. [[1]] [[3]] [[2]]

Sources:
[S8.1] Broadcom Inc. Announces Third Quarter Fiscal Year 2026 Financial Results and Quarterly Dividend — https://investors.broadcom.com/news-releases/news-release-details/broadcom-inc-announces-third-quarter-fiscal-year-2026-financial
[S8.2] Broadcom (AVGO) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript — https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/09/09/broadcom-avgo-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/
[S8.3] Earnings call transcript: Broadcom tops Q3 2026 estimates as AI sales surge By Investing.com — https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-broadcom-tops-q3-2026-estimates-as-ai-sales-surge-93CH-4886849

private_messages.content:
**Broadcom’s Q2 FY2026 AI semiconductor revenue was $10.8 billion**, up **143% year over year**, driven by demand for **custom AI accelerators (XPUs)** and **AI networking**; the fiscal quarter ended **May 3, 2026**. [[1, 2]] 

This result was modestly above Broadcom’s Q1 outlook for **$10.7 billion** in Q2 AI semiconductor revenue, an outperformance of roughly **$0.1 billion (0.9%)**. [[3]] 

For context, Q2 semiconductor-solutions revenue was **$15.009 billion**, meaning AI semiconductors represented about **72.0%** of the segment; total company revenue was **$22.187 billion**, making AI semiconductor revenue approximately **48.7%** of consolidated sales. [[1, 2]] 

Broadcom guided Q3 FY2026 AI semiconductor revenue to **$16.0 billion**, implying more than **200% year-over-year growth** and roughly **48% sequential growth** from Q2. [[1]] 

The key takeaway is that Broadcom’s AI revenue category encompasses both the **custom accelerator/XPU silicon** deployed by hyperscalers and the **networking components** required to scale those accelerator clusters; the company did not disclose a Q2 revenue split between the two categories. [[1]]

Sources:

function.arguments: {"query":"Broadcom Q1 FY2026 earnings call AI semiconductor revenue custom accelerator XPU networking breakdown"}

private_messages.content:
**Broadcom’s “AI semiconductor revenue” is a management-reported revenue category rather than a separately reported GAAP operating segment; it refers principally to sales of (1) customer-specific AI compute accelerators—called custom AI accelerators or XPUs—and (2) AI networking products.** [[1]] [[2]]

**XPU** is Broadcom management’s umbrella term for the purpose-built computing accelerators it supplies for customers’ AI data centers; these are customized alternatives to general-purpose GPU-based compute, exemplified in the call by shipments of Google’s Ironwood TPU and OpenAI’s Jalapeno accelerator. [[3]] [[2]]

**Custom accelerator revenue** therefore means revenue from these customer-designed or customer-tailored AI chips, while **AI networking revenue** encompasses the high-bandwidth interconnect needed to link AI accelerators—particularly Ethernet switching and optical interconnect products. [[2]] [[3]] 

For fiscal Q3 2026, ended August 2, 2026, Broadcom reported **$16.7 billion** of AI semiconductor revenue, up **221% year over year** and **54% sequentially**. [[1]] 

Management said XPU shipments increased by more than **3.5× year over year** and represented **73%** of Q3 AI revenue, while AI-networking revenue rose more than **2.5× year over year**. [[2]] 

This AI category was the principal growth driver within Broadcom’s Semiconductor Solutions segment, whose Q3 revenue was **$20.839 billion**, up **127% year over year**; total company revenue was **$29.591 billion**. [[1]] 

For fiscal Q4 2026, Broadcom guided to **$21.7 billion** of AI semiconductor revenue, implying **236% year-over-year growth**, and management’s Q3-call outlook was approximately **$58 billion** of AI revenue for full-year fiscal 2026. [[1]] [[3]] 

In short, the phrase should be read as Broadcom’s combined AI-chip platform revenue—**custom XPU/ASIC compute plus the Ethernet/optical fabric that scales those systems**—not as revenue from a single standalone “AI semiconductor” product or a formal reported segment. [[1]] [[3]] [[2]]

Sources:
[S8.1] Broadcom Inc. Announces Third Quarter Fiscal Year 2026 Financial Results and Quarterly Dividend — https://investors.broadcom.com/news-releases/news-release-details/broadcom-inc-announces-third-quarter-fiscal-year-2026-financial
[S8.2] Broadcom (AVGO) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript — https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/09/09/broadcom-avgo-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/
[S8.3] Earnings call transcript: Broadcom tops Q3 2026 estimates as AI sales surge By Investing.com — https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-broadcom-tops-q3-2026-estimates-as-ai-sales-surge-93CH-4886849
